rule: One entry per open data, source or integration issue. Entries are closed only with evidence (commit, run, file); never deleted. Gap-level detail lives in historical_gap_backlog.json; this register holds the issues and decisions behind those gaps.

issues.title: Annual-history refresh would remove 403 published observations
issues.detail: A live re-download of the Eurostat annual tables (releases 2026-11-11/13) revises 234 history observations (27 beyond the registered tolerance) and removes 403 observations in 16 series whose splice check against the frozen canonical years now fails (manufacturing share AT/HR/HU/PL/RO/SK, real GDP growth AT/HR/RO/SK, imports, trade balance and trade openness AT/HR); 8 series have revisions beyond tolerance (compensation per employee HR/RO, labour productivity HR/HU/RO/SK, trade balance and openness SK). Applying it would shrink published coverage.
options: keep the archived 2026-11-09 vintage in the annual history (current state)
deliberate canonical refresh in a release with model-impact review, after which the splice check passes again
owner rule change: a later vintage never de-admits already published history (admission frozen per vintage)

issues.title: Single-vintage reference carries the 2026-11-09 retrieval metadata
issues.evidence: a stage rebuild from the 2026-11-15 retrieval (releases 2026-11-11 / 2026-10-28) changes 0 of 882 values; only retrieved_at/dataset_updated_at would change
issues.detail: The published values equal the latest Eurostat release. Rebuilding only to refresh metadata is not worth a data run; the layer is rebuilt with the next applied annual refresh (the annual mode includes the single-vintage-reference unit).

issues.title: single-vintage-reference unit failed in live data-refresh mode
issues.evidence: scripts/historical-annual/build-single-vintage-reference.mjs (the builder no longer requires --offline; it never fetches); found by the live annual plan annual-refresh-20261116
issues.detail: The unit appends --offline only in offline runs, and the builder refused to run without it, so every live annual plan stopped on 'acquisition failed'.

issues.title: Vintage-held canonical years (301 periods) stay held in the spliced series
issues.detail: Resolved for research use by the unspliced reference layer; the main series converge only through a canonical refresh.

issues.title: High-frequency months after the frozen 2015+ store (146 periods)
issues.evidence: Eurostat prc_hicp_minr updated 2026-11-04 with flag 'e' for 2026-10 (AT, DE, HR, SK); task eurostat-oct-hicp-replan 2026-11-19; macro-driver unit blocked (owner decision 2026-09-30)
issues.detail: HICP/industrial production/unemployment/yields via the HF re-plan after the full October HICP release; BIS rates and FX need a deliberate macro-driver release.

issues.title: Canonical 2025 years for energy HICP and electricity prices (30 periods)
issues.evidence: historical_gap_backlog.json category A 'after the last canonical year'
issues.detail: observations.json is a frozen formal-model input; a deliberate canonical refresh is required.

issues.title: Unchecked source families (category B)
issues.detail: National statistical offices (no host registered), IMF (no host), OECD (licence review due), UN Comtrade before 2015 (not pursued 2026-11-11), Serbian national years before the Ministry of Finance bulletin. Any use must stay a separate national-definition series.

issues.title: Reference-layer field 'vintage' is a retrieval timestamp, not a statistical release vintage
issues.detail: The layer is concept 2 (latest revised values available at one retrieval per table), not concept 3 (point-in-time real-time vintages). Labels must say 'retrieved', and the layer must never be used as evidence of what was known at past publication dates. A vintage_definition header field is proposed for the next rebuild.

issues.title: Inherited frontend backlog (Codex-owned, not verified here)
issues.detail: Indicator search and category classification; arbitrary 2–10 country comparisons; vote-share versus seat-share presentation; map-first homepage quality; simplified research UI and natural language; Serbia election deep-link verification; production browser regression checks; Data Explorer integration of the single-vintage reference layer.
